title: 2026 Global
overview: 2026 Global M&A Outlook A global survey-based outlook on M&A, moving from a retrospective of 2025 to 2026 dealmaking themes and implications. Its main topics include strategic focus, differences between buyer types, portfolio simplification, AI-enabled deal execution, execution discipline, and industry-specific dynamics. The research surveyed 700 dealmakers across 20 countries and jurisdictions. A global outlook on mergers and acquisitions, reviewing 2025 and examining the 2026 M&A environment. It covers strategic focus, buyer risk appetites, portfolio simplification, AI-driven deal execution, execution discipline, industry-specific dynamics, and implications for dealmakers.
methods: The report’s findings are based on a global survey of corporate respondents.
key_findings: The report says private equity dealmakers are significantly more likely than corporate dealmakers to expect M&A pipeline activity to increase relative to 2025; corporates are described as having a more measured outlook, with fewer anticipating a material ac...
The report says the majority of anticipated transactions fall below the US$1B threshold, describing the expected rebound as led by mid-sized deals rather than megadeals.

The report describes private equity optimism as strongest in the US, while dealmakers outside the US—particularly corporates—face greater uncertainty related to growth, regulation and geopolitical exposure.
For “Types of deals under consideration — corporate vs. private equity,” acquisition of a full business is listed at 62% for corporate respondents and 69% for private equity respondents.

For “Types of deals under consideration — corporate vs. private equity,” carve-out acquisitions are listed at 21% for corporate respondents and 55% for private equity respondents, a displayed difference of +34 pts.

For “Types of deals under consideration — corporate vs. private equity,” minority-to-majority investments are listed at 18% for corporate respondents and 50% for private equity respondents, a displayed difference of +32 pts.

key_points: The survey included 700 M&A dealmakers across 20 countries and jurisdictions and was fielded from 19 December 2025 to 27 January 2026.
Respondents comprised 519 corporate dealmakers and 181 respondents from private equity firms; they were senior executives involved in M&A decision-making across 10 sectors.
